scope: All five cases are synthetic, author-reviewed examples. They do not use held-out data, a model, or another scoring attempt.
limitations: The tests check fixture facts and arithmetic, not natural-language truth or whether future models obey instructions. Each candidate and entry below is authored for this walkthrough, not generated by the system.

cases.user_case: 总分不满，但某一步已经正确完成
cases.original_operation: Filter region R, retain both authorized rows, sum their amounts; submit total=50.
cases.supported_observation: The filtered rows and arithmetic are correct under the explicit requirements. The submitted answer lacks the explicitly required currency field.
cases.uncertain: The aggregate score does not establish which field cost points or whether adding currency raises the score.
cases.bad_proposal: Redo the join and recompute the total because the score was low.

reflector_candidate.lesson: Retain the successful filter and sum; compare the final answer to explicitly required fields and add the missing currency label.
reflector_candidate.trigger: A task requests an aggregate and its currency.
reflector_candidate.scope_hint: Use the task-defined currency and required output schema, not arbitrary extra fields.

cases.evolver_reason: Keep the already correct filtering/summing. Add only a final required-field check because the final answer omitted currency; this is a supported proposal, not a demonstrated score repair.
cases.final_rule: For an aggregate task, filter and sum the authorized records according to the task. Preserve a verified total; before submission compare the result with the required output schema and attach its specified currency. Do not repeat correct work or add unrequested fields.

cases.user_case: 阈值未知，却被写成默认值
cases.original_operation: Read a latency of 18 minutes; the supplied task has no latency cutoff.
cases.supported_observation: A latency measurement is observed; no threshold or SLA breach is established.
cases.uncertain: Whether 18 minutes violates the applicable policy.
cases.bad_proposal: Use a default cutoff of 15 minutes and mandate escalation.

reflector_candidate.lesson: Obtain the applicable cutoff from an authorized policy before classifying a delay; if unavailable keep the classification unresolved.
reflector_candidate.trigger: A task needs a latency-policy decision.
reflector_candidate.scope_hint: The policy must apply to this entity and time window.

cases.evolver_reason: Replace the unsupported constant with a bounded policy lookup and an unresolved branch. The current data supports measuring latency, not a particular cutoff or benefit.
cases.final_rule: When a latency-policy decision is required, retain the measured latency and read the applicable authorized policy. Compare only if its entity, period and units match. If no threshold is supplied, report that the condition is unresolved or use the task-specified unknown outcome; do not invent a cutoff or mandatory escalation.

cases.user_case: 一个字段的定义被扩展成另一个字段的必要条件
cases.original_operation: Evaluate credit eligibility from credit balance, then use that result to gate the separately requested overdue flag.
cases.supported_observation: The explicit definitions govern distinct fields. This record can be ineligible for credit and still overdue.
cases.uncertain: The scalar score does not identify which field was penalized.
cases.bad_proposal: Only credit-eligible records may be marked overdue.

reflector_candidate.lesson: Evaluate each requested field under its applicable definition; introduce a dependency only if supplied by the definitions or logically entailed by applicable authorized facts.
reflector_candidate.trigger: A task requests multiple classification fields.
reflector_candidate.scope_hint: Keep credit eligibility and payment overdue distinct unless applicable definitions or authorized facts support a dependency; the supplied counterexample rules out the proposed dependency here.

cases.evolver_reason: Preserve the correct credit eligibility calculation; remove the unsupported gate on overdue and use its supplied due-date/unpaid definition.
cases.final_rule: List the task-defined inputs for each requested field. Evaluate credit eligibility from credit balance and overdue from due date and unpaid amount. Keep the results independent unless applicable definitions or authorized facts logically establish a dependency; retain the premises and check counterexamples instead of linking fields merely because they appear related.

cases.user_case: 一天多次运行，运行次数与天数不同
cases.original_operation: Count failed execution records and use the count as failed days.
cases.supported_observation: The authorized records contain two failures on one UTC calendar day.
cases.uncertain: This fixture shows a metric mismatch, not how much of any aggregate score it explains.
cases.bad_proposal: Set failed_days to the number of failed runs in every recurring batch task.

reflector_candidate.lesson: Count distinct task-defined dates for a day metric, preserving entity and timezone.
reflector_candidate.trigger: A task asks for failed-day counts from run records.
reflector_candidate.scope_hint: A run count equals a day count only when the relevant records have at most one run per defined date.

cases.evolver_reason: Retain the observed failures and entity filter; change only the aggregation grain from executions to distinct UTC dates, because the task explicitly asks for days.
cases.final_rule: For a failed-day metric, filter the requested entity/window and failed status, convert timestamps to the task-defined date basis, and count distinct dates. Use execution count for an execution metric. Do not substitute run count for day count unless the one-run-per-date premise is established.

cases.user_case: 候选保留了条件，最终合并正文却丢失条件

authorized_facts.candidate_condition: One-to-one order/customer mapping for the same entity and reporting period is verified.

cases.original_operation: Join order amounts to customer mapping in a training scene with a verified one-to-one mapping.
cases.supported_observation: The candidate limits direct reconciliation to a verified mapping, entity and period; removing those premises permits double counting.
cases.uncertain: The original total score does not prove the join is universally valid or that the proposed checks improve scores.
cases.bad_proposal: Merge into a general rule: join orders to customer mapping and sum the resulting rows.

reflector_candidate.lesson: Reconcile joined totals only after verifying the mapping is one-to-one for the same entity and reporting period.
reflector_candidate.scope_hint: Same entity and period; verify unique mapping keys before aggregating.

cases.evolver_reason: Preserve the useful join and all its conditions in the final procedure. A duplicate-key counterexample shows why a broader unconditional rule would double count.
cases.final_rule: For order/customer reconciliation, first check entity, reporting period and mapping-key uniqueness. If the one-to-one premise holds, join and sum. If duplicate keys remain, inspect the task-defined join relationship or leave reconciliation unresolved; do not silently multiply or deduplicate amounts.
